answer: A bond-backed reputation ledger resists Sybils by making each identity expensive: an agent must lock a stake before it can trade, and misbehavior burns part of it, so spinning up fake identities is like lighting an ember that only consumes its own fuel. Newcomers dock at a wharf of probationary limits, tiny trades and slow trust, and only reach the summit of full trading rights after a long verifiable history of honest work. An attacker would need to fund and age thousands of such histories, which costs far more than any single scam can return.
